title: The evaluation-normalized native closed comparison remains valid after changing from the chosen closure to D.k and from internal modules to section mo
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum D (finite field k₀ of characteristic p with its specified algebraic closure k), a prime l≠p, a normalized realization Family R, and a separated finite-type k₀-scheme X₀ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-sf-adic-realization-isomorphism-data]. Let Y₀=X₀×_{k₀}AlgebraicClosure(k₀), Y=X₀×_{k₀}k, and h:Y₀≅Y the specified closure isomorphism. Let U₀ be the native derived Weil forgetful functor, E the section-module equivalence in R.data(Y), V=R h_* followed by D(E), U=U₀ followed by V, and F the termwise complex functor E_Ch∘(h_*)_Ch. Use the ordinary section-module closed structure S and symmetry specified by that realization, including its K-flat total-tensor models. All derived categories here are unbounded and ambient, with the coefficient and size conventions in the realization, not only their bounded constructible subcategories [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

There exist a NativeClosedComparison N and its full Compatible laws [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models], natural isomorphisms v_{A,B}:V(A⊗_N B)≅VA⊗_S VB and t_{K,L}:U(K⊗_N L)≅UK⊗_S UL, and e:U(1_N)≅1_S, with these properties. Write composition in diagrammatic order using ';'.

(1) Normalization on every pair of ordinary native K-flat complexes P,Q: FP,FQ are K-flat. For every complex T there is a natural factor a_T:V(Q₀T)≅Q_s(FT), whose inverse is exactly λ_T, the fixed section localization-factor inverse followed by D(E) of the actual right-derived unit Q(h_*T)→R h_*(Q₀T). There is a chain isomorphism c_{P,Q}:F(Tot_o(P,Q))≅Tot_s(FQ,FP). Here Tot_o is the actual reversed-curried ordinary tensor total: its (p,q) summand is Q^q⊗P^p and its differential is the P differential plus (-1)^p times the Q differential; Tot_s is the usual total with its displayed factor order. For every local pure section x∈(FQ)^q, y∈(FP)^p, c sends the transported (p,q) summand generator x⊗y to (-1)^(pq) times the (q,p) generator x⊗y. If m_o(P,Q):Q₀Q⊗_N Q₀P≅Q₀Tot_o(P,Q) is N's specified ordinary model and m_s(FQ,FP):Q_sTot_s(FQ,FP)≅Q_sFQ⊗_S Q_sFP is S's specified model, then
V(m_o(P,Q)^{-1});v_{Q₀Q,Q₀P}=a_{Tot_o(P,Q)};Q_s(c_{P,Q});m_s(FQ,FP);(λ_Q⊗_Sλ_P).

(2) t_{K,L}=V(N.tensorComparison_{K,L});v_{U₀K,U₀L}. The comparison t and unit e respect associators and both unitors: the path from U((K⊗L)⊗M) through U's associator and t_{K,L⊗M} then 1⊗t_{L,M} equals the path through t_{K⊗L,M}, then t_{K,L}⊗1, then S's associator. Moreover U(leftUnitor_K)=t_{1,K};(e⊗1);leftUnitor_{UK}, and U(rightUnitor_K)=t_{K,1};(1⊗e);rightUnitor_{UK}. They preserve symmetry: U(β^N_{K,L});t_{L,K}=t_{K,L};β^S_{UK,UL}.

(3) For every native derived K,L, the specific map U(H_N(K,L))→H_S(UK,UL) obtained by S-transposing t_{H_N(K,L),K}^{-1};U(ev^N_{K,L}) is an isomorphism, natural contravariantly in K and covariantly in L. This is the evaluation-defined sectionHomComparison. No invertibility of a bidual arrow is asserted.

STATEMENT-DISPUTED correction to the imported Lean TransportNormalized: its unsigned generator formula must contain the factor (-1)^(pq) displayed in (1). All other clauses of NativeSectionClosed.Comparison are retained. The unsigned formula fails the chain-map equation already for P=(O→O) in degrees 0,1 with differential identity and Q=O in degree 1 over a nonempty coefficient point: the source differential is +1 and the target differential is -1, while the demanded components of c are both +1.

proof.text: Use the Frobenius-action resolutions theorem for the twisted ringed-site presentation, exactness, products and K-injective preservation of U₀. Fix the canonical derived closed structure and its specified tensor-Hom adjunction by the ringed closed and adjunction theorems. The ringed two-injective theorem now applies, including its native specialization, and supplies the native and ordinary derived Hom bifunctors with their two-injective representatives. Apply the row-sign representative conversion to these very bifunctors and their derived comparison, obtaining M and eta with NativeHomRepresentativeCompatibility. The conversion retains the derived arrows, changing only the product-Hom convention. The hypotheses are exactly finite k₀, l away from its characteristic and separated finite-type X₀; finite type over a field also gives the quasi-compactness required by the model theorem. Work throughout in the native derived category of module pairs, not pairs in an already formed derived category.

proof.text: Choose the ordinary tensor model explicitly before choosing its adjunction. Let B=ordinaryTensorBifunctor and let s_{P,Q}:Tot_o(P,Q)≅Tot(Q⊗P) be the inverse of the signed flip for B, identifying B.flip with the standard tensor through the canonical balanced tensor isomorphism. Its (p,q) component is (-1)^(pq) times the (q,p) inclusion. The same isomorphism identifies the native acyclic K-flat test with the standard one. Use the generic derived-monoidal theorem for the native module-object category and its two-variable derived-tensor statement; these fix its canonical localization tensorator. Equivalently its section presentation has the ringed native tensor maps. The canonical localization tensorator μ_{Q,P}:Q₀Q⊗Q₀P≅Q₀Tot(Q⊗P) is invertible when P is K-flat. Set m⁰(P,Q)=μ_{Q,P};Q₀(s_{P,Q}^{-1}). It is natural by naturality of μ and s. Apply the representative-currying theorem to this particular m⁰ and M.ordinaryRepresentatives. Use its natural bijections e as the adjunction bijections defining S_o on the canonical monoidal structure: unit and counit are the inverse-bijection images of identities, so their triangle identities follow from inverse bijectivity and naturality. The stated inverse-currying naturality gives evaluation_naturality. Thus S_o.transpose=e exactly. The theorem's unsigned equation is NativeAdjunctionNormalization for m⁰. Choose the canonical Koszul symmetry and swap s_{P,Q};β_{Q,P};s_{Q,P}^{-1}; its three homogeneous signs multiply to (-1)^(pq). The localization tensorator's braiding equation gives the required model/swap square. Hence m⁰ and this swap witness NativeOrdinaryTensorModels for this specific S_o, whose monoidal constraints are canonical.

proof.text: Apply the native tensor lift to M, eta and the specific S_o, its canonical symmetry and ordinary models from step 2. Keep the lift's native and ordinary units and tau. In its uncurry identity set f=id_H: uncurrying the identity is evaluation, so eta is exactly the mapped-evaluation transpose. Closed transposition gives evaluation and bidual compatibility and bidual naturality, without bidual invertibility. Together with the lift's coherence, symmetry and retained representative square this gives N and its full Compatible laws. The existential witness selected by N.ordinaryTensorModels.choose is not assumed to be m⁰. Its specification and m⁰ both satisfy NativeAdjunctionNormalization for the same unchanged S_o and M.ordinaryRepresentatives. Apply fixed-adjunction model uniqueness: for every K-flat P,Q the actual selected m_o(P,Q) equals μ_{Q,P};Q₀(s_{P,Q}^{-1}). Thus m_o(P,Q)^{-1}=Q₀(s_{P,Q});μ_{Q,P}^{-1}. This equality pins exactly the map used by TransportNormalized, even if a different existential proof was stored in N.

proof.text: The specified equivalence of algebraic closures is an isomorphism over k₀; its base change h has inverse the base change of the inverse (the two composites are identities by the fiber-product universal property). The pro-etale isomorphism lemma reindexes objects and covers and gives inverse sheaf equivalences. Reindexing preserves the pulled-back coefficient ring: on an object (Z→Y) the ring consists of the same continuous finite-subextension-valued functions on |Z|, so the coefficient isomorphism and its inverse are identities on those functions. This equivalence is continuous and cocontinuous. The ringed tensor-restriction theorem therefore supplies its invertible pure-tensor and rank-one unit maps. Under the internal/section operations comparison it is the actual internal h_*. Thus h_* is an additive exact equivalence with the indicated tensor maps, not a replacement direct image.

proof.text: Apply the internal-section tensor comparison to E on the small pro-etale site in the coefficient universe fixed by R. It is the realization's exact section equivalence and sends local m⊗n to m⊗n. Compose it with h_* to obtain the additive exact symmetric strong monoidal equivalence F on modules, with exact inverse obtained by reversing the two equivalences. Its coefficient unit map is the composite of the two prescribed rank-one unit maps. Associativity, both unit and symmetry diagrams can be checked on a local tensor m⊗n⊗z (respectively a scalar times m, or m⊗n): both paths have the same images, and balanced tensors generate locally before sheafification. These checks also fix the maps on sheafified tensors.

proof.text: Apply the flip leaf first in the source: with B=ordinaryTensorBifunctor, its inverse is s_{P,Q}:Tot_o(P,Q)≅Tot(Q⊗P), with the canonical identification of B.flip with standard tensor. Apply F_Ch to s. Only now apply the exact-monoidal-equivalence theorem's standard-total map τ_{Q,P}:F_Ch Tot(Q⊗P)≅Tot(FQ⊗FP). Define c_{P,Q}=F_Ch(s_{P,Q});τ_{Q,P}. This uses τ solely on the standard total, exactly as its statement permits. The source flip contributes (-1)^(pq); τ sends each same-indexed pure tensor x⊗y to x⊗y. Therefore c has the signed local formula in (1), with target indices (q,p), and is natural. The inverse flip identifies NativeOrdinaryKFlat with the standard acyclic-test condition. The exact-monoidal-equivalence theorem preserves that condition and its equivalent two-sided quasi-isomorphism test. Hence FP,FQ have the required target K-flatness, with no flat-term or boundedness hypothesis. Tensor is additive and preserves the countable coproducts on both module categories in the specified coefficient universe.

Exact-functor derived comparison makes the actual right-derived unit for h_* invertible on every complex. Combine its D(E)-image with the fixed section localization factor to obtain λ_T and set a_T=λ_T^{-1}, naturally for all T. Resolving tensor descent for E∘h_* gives the derived equivalence V, a coherent symmetric tensor comparison v and its localized coefficient unit. Its ringed-site hypothesis is met by passing internal modules to section modules at both ends. Both monoidal structures are the canonical ones carrying the canonical models; the theorem also identifies the supplied realization models and covers all K-flat representatives without flat terms.
For K-flat P,Q, step 3 pins the actual chosen model: m_o^{-1}=Q₀(s);μ^{-1}. Consequently the left side of (1) is V(Q₀s);V(μ^{-1});v. The standard resolving-descent square for (Q,P) rewrites its last two factors as a_{Tot(Q⊗P)};Q_s(τ_{Q,P});m_s(FQ,FP);(λ_Q⊗λ_P). Naturality of a replaces V(Q₀s);a_{Tot(Q⊗P)} by a_{Tot_o};Q_s(F_Chs). The middle composite is Q_s(c) by step 6. This is exactly (1), with the actual .choose model and the prescribed λ, without assuming that an arbitrary model is canonical. Coherence of v comes from descent on the fixed canonical monoidal structures, independently of the Hom adjunction.

proof.text: Define t_{K,L}=V(tau_{K,L});v_{U₀K,U₀L}, and define e by V of N's coefficient-unit comparison followed by V's coefficient-unit comparison. These are natural isomorphisms. Paste the two associator diagrams for tau and v; naturality of v moves V(tau) through the middle tensor maps, giving exactly the two associator paths in (2). Pasting the two left-unit diagrams and then the two right-unit diagrams gives the displayed unit equations. Similarly insert V(tau_{L,K});v after U of native symmetry, apply symmetry compatibility of tau, then that of v: the result is t_{K,L};β^S. Thus tensor_transport, coherent and symmetric all hold. These are identities of composites, so no further geometric or resolution assertion enters this step.

proof.text:
The canonical evaluation-transpose Hom comparison b_{A,B}:V(H_o(A,B))→H_S(VA,VB) is invertible by the monoidal-equivalence Hom theorem, since V is the strong monoidal equivalence constructed in step 7. That theorem uses left-tensor evaluation; conjugate with the preserved symmetries to express it in the Hom-first evaluation convention used here. Put d_{K,L}=V(eta_{K,L});b_{U₀K,U₀L}; it is natural and invertible. Its evaluation composite is
(d_{K,L}⊗1);ev_S = (V(eta_{K,L})⊗1);v_{H_o(U₀K,U₀L),U₀K}^{-1};V(ev_o)
= v_{U₀H_N(K,L),U₀K}^{-1};V((eta_{K,L}⊗1);ev_o)
= v^{-1};V(tau_{H_N(K,L),K}^{-1});U(ev_N)
= t_{H_N(K,L),K}^{-1};U(ev_N).
The second equality is naturality of v and the third is N.Compatible's evaluation square. Uniqueness of the specified tensor-Hom transpose identifies d with sectionHomComparison for this very t. Hence the required hom_isIso holds for all ambient K,L, without a dualizability, constructibility or reflexivity assumption. Together with steps 2–3, 6–8 this supplies every field of the corrected Comparison.
